newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Key Albanian party says to take part in election.
newsitem.headline: Key Albanian party says to take part in election.

text.p: Albania's second-largest political party, the Socialist Party, on Thursday said it had decided to run in June 29 elections, lifting a planned boycott that threatened to stop the election taking place.
The decision ends a deadlock over the elections, regarded as vital to stop Albania plunging back into violence and anarchy.
"We will take part in the election," a party official told Reuters after a day-long meeting of its national council.
He stressed that during the campaign the party would continuously check to ensure the poll would be free and fair.
The agreement of the Socialist Party was the biggest hurdle to overcome to get the elections on track and is likely to be followed by approval from other parties to run in the vote.

The parties threatened to boycott the vote over election rules which they said favoured President Sali Berisha and his former ruling Democratic Party. The Socialists, the main rival to Berisha, pulled out of the previous election in May 1996, accusing the Democrats of rigging the vote.
